How the scores are computed

Source: vignettes/articles/methods.Rmd
methods.Rmd

The three criteria compare a training matrix X (n × p) with a test matrix X0 (n0 × p). The v2 code formed matrices with n0 rows and n0 columns at every step of the search. The v3 code uses matrices whose size is the smaller of n and p. The values are the same.

Let λ = 1/p for the r-score and PEV, and λ = 1 for CD, and write G = X’X (p × p).

The push-through identity

The ridge solution can be written in a primal or a dual form:

𝐗′(𝐗𝐗′+λ𝐈n)−1=(𝐗′𝐗+λ𝐈p)−1𝐗′ \mathbf{X}'(\mathbf{X}\mathbf{X}' + \lambda \mathbf{I}_n)^{-1} = (\mathbf{X}'\mathbf{X} + \lambda \mathbf{I}_p)^{-1}\mathbf{X}'

The left side needs an n × n inverse, the right side a p × p inverse. v3 picks the smaller one:

  • p ≤ n (primal): everything is a p × p matrix, and the test set enters only through X0’X0.
  • p > n (dual): everything is an n × n matrix.

r-score

With M = (G + λI)^-1 G, S0 = c² X0’X0, and c = 1 − 1/n0 (the constant of v2.4.2, kept as published):

q1=n0−1+tr⁡(𝐒0),q2=tr⁡(𝐌𝐁𝐒0)+tr⁡(𝐌′𝐒0𝐌),q12=ctr⁡(𝐗0′𝐗0𝐌) q_1 = n_0 - 1 + \operatorname{tr}(\mathbf{S}_0), \quad q_2 = \operatorname{tr}(\mathbf{M}\mathbf{B}\mathbf{S}_0) + \operatorname{tr}(\mathbf{M}'\mathbf{S}_0\mathbf{M}), \quad q_{12} = c\,\operatorname{tr}(\mathbf{X}_0'\mathbf{X}_0\mathbf{M})

and the r-score is q₁₂ / √(q₁ q₂), with B = (G + λI)^-1. The test set enters only through the p × p matrix X0’X0, which the search computes once when the test set is fixed.

PEV and CD

  • PEV is tr(B X0e’X0e) with an intercept column added (X0e), a p × p trace in the primal form.
  • CD is the mean over test rows of x_i’ B G B x_i / x_i’x_i, a quadratic form per row, with no n0 × n0 matrix.

What does not change

  • The criterion values equal those of v2.4.2: to about 1e-7, the accuracy of the single-precision numbers v2 returned. The tests compare against an independent R transcription of the v2 formulas to 1e-9, and against values recorded from v2.4.2.
  • The search moves, the order of the random numbers, the default number of iterations, and the stopping rule are those of v2.4.2. With options(TSDFGS.legacy_float = TRUE) and the same seed, optTrain() returns the training sets recorded from v2.4.2 for all twelve routes (with or without sub-populations, targeted or not, three criteria).

Where the time goes

Per move, v2 spent O(n0² p + n³) operations; v3 spends O(n0 p² + p³) for an untargeted search and O(p³ + n p²) for a targeted one, plus the cost of copying the training rows. The slow case for both is large p together with large n; reducing p with the leading PCs is the practical remedy, and it changes the criterion, so choose it before comparing results.

The C++ code uses Eigen through the RcppEigen package. R is the interface: it checks inputs, draws the starting set, and returns the result.
